props.gloss_en: Beit Hillel: every person reads as he is -- 'and when you walk on the way'
Beit Hillel: 'when you lie down and when you rise' denotes time -- the hour when people lie down and the hour when they rise

Beit Shammai: had the verse meant only time it would say 'in the morning and in the evening'; 'when you lie down and when you rise' means at the hour of lying down -- actually lying down, and at the hour of rising -- actually risen
'when you sit in your house' -- to the exclusion of one engaged in a mitzva
'and when you walk on the way' -- to the exclusion of a groom
from here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt [from the Shema]
and one who marries a widow is obligated

had the Torah meant to obligate in every case it would write 'when sitting and when walking'; 'when YOU sit and when YOU walk' -- in your own sitting and walking you are obligated, in that of a mitzva you are exempt
this one [who marries a virgin] is preoccupied, that one [who marries a widow] is not -- the groom's exemption is grounded in preoccupation
Rav: a mourner is obligated in all the mitzvot stated in the Torah
except tefillin, from which the mourner is exempt
for 'splendour' is said of them -- 'bind your splendour upon you' (Ezek 24:17)
there [the groom] is preoccupied with a mitzva's preoccupation; here [the shipwrecked man] with a voluntary one
Beit Shammai need the phrase to exclude agents on a mitzva errand
Beit Hillel: from that itself it follows that [one not on a mitzva errand] reads even on the way

schemas.gloss_en: כי דרך: מה דרך רשות, אף כל רשות -- as the 'way' of the verse is voluntary, so all [whom the verse obligates] are engaged in the voluntary; one engaged in a mitzva is excluded

grounds.gloss_en: מי לא עסקינן דקא אזיל לדבר מצוה, ואפילו הכי אמר רחמנא ליקרי -- does the verse's 'way' not cover one walking for a mitzva too, whom the Torah still tells to read? then 'way' is not the voluntary case, and nothing follows from it

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי אפילו כונס את האלמנה נמי -- if so, one who marries a widow should also be exempt; yet the baraita obligates him

answered_by.gloss_en: האי טריד והאי לא טריד -- the one is preoccupied, the other is not (= p_tarid)

objections.gloss_en: אי משום טרדא, אפילו טבעה ספינתו בים נמי! וכי תימא הכי נמי -- אלמה אמר רבי אבא בר זבדא אמר רב: אבל חייב בכל המצות האמורות בתורה חוץ מן התפילין -- if preoccupation exempts, one whose ship sank should be exempt; and if you say so indeed, why is Rav's mourner obligated in every mitzva?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם טריד טרדא דמצוה, הכא טריד טרדא דרשות -- the groom's is a mitzva's preoccupation, the shipwrecked man's a voluntary one (= p_tirda_demitzva)
